One value. Test: what is the most formal setting where this item would not look out of place? Start from the anchor items for each level. Smart-casual is the default for polished daywear: a piece someone would wear to lunch, a cafe or a relaxed office is smart-casual even when it is comfortable. Choose casual only when the item is built for home, the gym, the beach or sport, or is deliberately relaxed streetwear (hoodie, graphic T-shirt, joggers, distressed denim, slides). When torn between casual and smart-casual, choose smart-casual. Move up one level for satin, silk, velvet, lace or heavy embellishment. Move down one level for fleece, distressing or a large logo; jersey or denim alone does not move an item down. Never move more than one level from the anchor. For an item that spans levels (a plain belt, sunglasses, a simple leather tote), pick the middle of the range and give medium confidence.

Built for home, errands, the gym, the beach or sport, or deliberately relaxed. Clothing: hoodies, sweatshirts, graphic or logo T-shirts, joggers, denim shorts, distressed or baggy jeans, swimwear, activewear. Shoes and bags: sports and chunky trainers, slides, flip-flops, canvas totes, backpacks, belt bags.

Fits lunch with friends or a relaxed office. Clothing: plain fine-fabric T-shirts, polo shirts, knitwear, dark or clean-wash jeans, chinos, casual shirts, tailored shorts, day dresses, everyday kaftans. Shoes and bags: loafers, clean leather trainers, ballet flats, espadrilles, leather totes, shoulder and crossbody bags.

Fits a business meeting or an upscale restaurant. Clothing: blazers, tailored trousers, shirting, pencil skirts, structured midi dresses, plain tailored abayas. Shoes, bags, jewellery: pumps, block heels, Oxfords, structured top-handle bags, fine everyday jewellery.

Fits a wedding, an Eid gathering or a gala dinner. Clothing: suits, cocktail dresses, embellished kaftans and abayas, silk or satin occasion dresses. Shoes, bags, jewellery: stilettos, embellished sandals, clutches, statement jewellery.
Fits an event with a black-tie dress code. Clothing: tuxedos, floor-length evening gowns. Shoes and bags: satin or crystal evening shoes, minaudieres, patent dress shoes.

One to three values, strongest first. Decide formality first. Test for each value: would a stylist reach for this item for that occasion without being told to? If it only "could work", leave it out. Everyday and work often go together: a smart-casual piece that is opaque and neat passes both tests, so give both. Evening describes time and mood, wedding guest a dress code, special occasion any celebration; a formal piece can carry all three only when each test passes on its own. Everyday never sits beside evening, wedding guest or special occasion. If no test passes clearly, answer unknown; do not fall back to everyday.
Tag when formality is 1 or 2 and there is no occasion-specific design. Do not tag when formality is 4 or 5, or the piece is heavily embellished.

Tag when formality is 2 or 3 and the piece is opaque and neat enough for a relaxed office. Clothing: tailoring, shirting, knitwear, polo shirts, dark jeans, chinos, plain day dresses, midi skirts. Shoes: loafers, flats, pumps, clean leather trainers, low to mid heels. Bags: totes, shoulder bags and structured bags that hold daily essentials. Accessories: watches, belts and fine everyday jewellery. Do not tag when sheer, heavily embellished, mini length, distressed, sportswear, or formality 1.
Tag when formality is 3 to 5 with evening cues: satin, velvet, sequins, metallics, dark or jewel tones, high heels, clutches. Do not tag daywear cotton or linen, even when smart.

Tag when formality is 4, or 3 in a dressy fabric: occasion dresses, gowns, dressy kaftans, suits, dressy heels, clutches. Do not tag casual fabrics, or a piece that reads as bridal. A white dress is excluded only if it reads as bridal.
Tag when formality is 4 or 5, for any formal celebration. This is the broad value: use it when the piece is formal but no narrower value fits better. Do not tag when formality is 3 or below.

Tag when the text names Ramadan or Eid, or the piece is a dressy kaftan, abaya or jalabiya: long, opaque, with rich fabric or embellishment. Do not tag a piece that is merely modest, and do not tag a plain everyday abaya.
Tag when the text names a GCC national day, or the design deliberately uses a national flag's colours or emblems. Do not tag when colours match by coincidence, such as a plain red dress.
Tag swimwear, cover-ups, linen, crochet, raffia, slides, espadrilles and straw bags. Do not tag a light summer item with no holiday cue.
Tag luggage, weekend bags, passport holders and travel accessories, or clothing the text describes as made for travel. Do not tag an item just because it is comfortable.
Tag performance activewear, performance trainers, sports bags and skiwear. Do not tag fashion trainers or athletic-looking streetwear.

One to three values, or all-season on its own. Judge by how heavy the fabric is first and by coverage second. In the Gulf a long loose garment in a light fabric is warm-weather clothing, so long sleeves alone never mean cold. Use all-season for anything worn or used all year: a plain T-shirt, jeans, leather trainers, and bags, jewellery and accessories whose material is not seasonal. All-season stands alone; never combine it with warm, transitional or cold, and never list all three of those in its place. Use warm, transitional or cold only when the item clearly belongs to one or two of them. If the fabric of a garment cannot be read from the text or the photo, answer unknown.
Light, breathable fabric or open construction: linen, cotton poplin, chiffon, light silk; sleeveless and short-sleeved pieces; light kaftans and abayas; sandals, slides, raffia bags.
Medium weight, or an outer layer worn without a coat: denim, jersey, light knits, blazers, trench coats, leather jackets, loafers, ankle boots.
Heavy or insulating: wool coats, heavy cashmere knits, puffers, shearling, knee boots, gloves, skiwear.
Not tied to a season: worn or used all year. A plain T-shirt, jeans, leather trainers; a leather bag, a watch, fine jewellery, sunglasses with no seasonal material. Stands alone.

One or two values. The first is the short answer to "what style is this?"; add a second only when the piece is clearly both. To separate classic from minimalist, ask two questions in order. First, is the shape long-established and recognisable (see classic)? If yes, classic comes first. Second, is the piece stripped back: solid colour, no logo, no decoration, little visible hardware? If the shape is not a heritage shape and the piece is stripped back, it is minimalist. If both are true, give classic first and minimalist second. A pinstriped blazer is classic only; a plain column dress is minimalist only; a plain black blazer is classic then minimalist. Bold works in daylight; glamorous is for an occasion. Minimalist and bold/statement never go together.

A modern, stripped-back piece: clean lines, solid colour, no visible logo, no embellishment, little visible hardware. Examples: a column dress, a plain slip skirt, a seamless knit, an unbranded smooth leather tote. Not anything with a print, pattern or decoration, and not first choice for a heritage shape (that is classic first).

A long-established, recognisable shape: trench coat, blazer, white or Oxford shirt, straight-leg jeans, crew-neck cashmere knit, pumps, loafers, a top-handle bag, pearls, a round or rectangular dress watch. Stripes, checks and a small heritage logo are allowed. Not a classic shape in a loud colour or exaggerated cut.
Soft and delicate: ruffles, lace, florals, bows, tulle, pastels, puff sleeves. Not a floral print on a sharp, tailored shape.
One loud element that leads: saturated colour, oversized shape, large print, sculptural form. Not shine or sparkle on an occasion piece; that is glamorous.
Relaxed and crafted: crochet, fringe, embroidery, paisley, tiered maxi shapes, earthy tones, raffia. Not a plain maxi dress.
Hoodies, graphic T-shirts, oversized fits, cargo shapes, chunky trainers, prominent logos, caps. Not performance sportswear with no street styling.
Shine and drama: sequins, crystals, metallics, satin, body-defining cuts, high heels. Not a plain piece in a formal fabric.

A fashion piece designed around coverage: abayas, kaftans, long-sleeved maxi dresses, layered sets, with coverage as the design idea. It is a style, not a measurement: an item that merely has long sleeves does not qualify.
Athletic references: track stripes, technical fabrics, polos, trainers. Performance activewear counts. Not a hoodie with a large logo; that is streetwear.
One value. A print is not embellishment; it belongs to pattern. Hardware that does a job (a zip, a plain clasp) does not count.

One value, optional. If the text names two colours for the product, the second is the secondary colour: use it and quote the words. If the text names only one colour or none, look at the photos: the secondary colour is the second most prominent colour on the product itself, such as a contrast panel, trim, lining that shows, or a second colour in a print. Ignore hardware, the background, the model and other products in the shot. It must differ from the primary colour. Map the colour to a value the same way as for colour_primary. If the product is clearly one colour, answer not applicable.

One value: the main fastening that opens and closes the garment. Use what the text states first; otherwise what the photos show. Never assume a zip. Trousers, jeans and shorts follow their own rule: if there is a button or press stud at the waistband, stated in the text or visible in a photo, the closure is button, even when the text also names a zip fly. When the text names only a zip for one of these, look at the photos for a waist button before answering. Choose zip for trousers, jeans and shorts only when there is a zip and no waist button, such as a side or back zip. For every other garment, if more than one fastening is present, choose the one that opens the garment, not a decorative one. If the text does not name a fastening and none can be seen in the photos, answer unknown.
Buttons or press studs do the fastening: shirts, cardigans, blazers. Also trousers, jeans and shorts with a button or press stud at the waistband, whether the fly below it is buttoned or zipped.

The text says zip or zipped, or a zip is visible in a photo: back zip, side zip, zip-front jacket. On trousers, jeans and shorts, only when there is no button or press stud at the waistband. Never chosen by default.
No fastening: pulled over the head or up over the hips. T-shirts, jumpers, elasticated or drawstring waists on stretch fabric, slip dresses with no zip mentioned or visible.
One side crosses over the other and is held by a tie or inner button: wrap dresses, wrap skirts, wrap tops, robes.
Ties, a belt or a lace-up do the fastening on a piece that does not wrap: tie-front tops, lace-up backs, halter ties, tie-side bottoms.
Hook-and-eye or hook-and-bar is the main fastening: bras, corsets, bustiers, some tailored trousers when the text says so.
